catalog_quote: The most superficial observation about Catalan stress is that words are either unstressed, or else stressed on one of the last three syllables. ... Although oxytones are more common than paroxytones, and proparoxytones are least common, there is no clear correlation between place of stress or any other general property of morphemes. ... Polymorphemic words show only one stress on the surface, the position being determined by the inherent properties of their constituent morphemes. ... [p.26, on Wheeler 1974's rule analysis:] Two rules, MSR and Minor SR, assign stress to lexical items. One rule assigns stress to a last nonfinal vowel (i.e., / __C0 [+segm]#) ... The Minor SR assigns stress in similar though not identical conditions, one syllable further back. ... Items are marked either [+E] or [-E]. ... [pp.33-34:] I will present a system that follows from a quite different assumption, na…
sweep_summary: Catalan (stan1289) is in the catalog as 'lexical' on Mascaró 1976 (with GIEC 2016 fetched sources earlier as co-deciding). Of the 11 title-hits, only three concern word stress: Faust & Torres-Tamarit 2017 (Glossa, open; fetched sources via the Wayback copy of the HAL author PDF) gives a clean first-hand statement — regular stress = final in C-final nominals, penult in V-final ones, lexical stress anywhere in a right-edge three-syllable window, morphology mostly irrelevant — which confirms the catalog coding; Torres-Tamarit & Pons-Moll 2015 (Going Romance talk, published 2019 in J. Linguistics, paywalled; abstract read) adds Balearic verb+enclitic stress shift and calls the unmarked nominal pattern a right-aligned moraic trochee (refines); Roca 1999 (Eurotyp Romance-stress survey, De Gruyter, paywalled, no open copy anywhere) is the one unread item worth acquiring (priority high). Cabré & Prieto 2004 (Probus; author copy fetched sources from the archived UPF prosody site) is about glide formation but states Catalan's preference for trochaic feet and avoidance of antepenultimate stress (consistent). The rest are intonation/phrasing/syllabification work (Prieto & Rigau 2007 and Vanrell et al. 2014 fetched sources and read, silent on word stress; Feldhausen 2008/2010, Vanrell 2013 and Torres-Tamarit & Pons-Moll 2012 judged from abstracts/titles, none read in full; Cabré & Prieto 2005 paywalled, low priority). No item contradicts the catalog; nothing read supersedes Mascaró 1976 as deciding source, but Faust & Torres-Tamarit 2017 should be added as an open, modern supporting citation. discovery used Unpaywall, Crossref, HAL and Wayback CDX APIs instead.

new_statements.quote: In Catalan, nominal forms have either regular or lexical stress. Regular stress falls on the last vowel if the word is consonant-final (11a) and on the penultimate vowel if the word is vowel-final (11b). [...] Lexical stress can appear on any vowel within a right-oriented three-syllable window. Penultimate stress is exceptional in consonant-final words (12a), final stress is exceptional in vowel-final words (12b), and there are also words ending in a vowel or a consonant that show antepenultimate stress (12c). [...] Morphological structure is in most cases irrelevant for stress assignment.
new_statements.citation: Faust, Noam and Torres-Tamarit, Francesc (2017). Stress and final /n/ deletion in Catalan: Combining Strict CV and OT. Glossa: a journal of general linguistics 2(1): 63, 1-23. doi:10.5334/gjgl.64.
new_statements.locator: §2.2 'Stress in Catalan', Art. 63 pp.7-8 (txt lines 999-1011), with examples (11)-(12)
new_statements.reading: A concise modern statement by two native-speaker phonologists: Catalan nominal stress is lexically specified within a right-edge three-syllable window, with a strong statistical default of final stress in consonant-final words and penultimate stress in vowel-final words; verbs are set aside. This matches the catalog's 'lexical' coding (Mascaró 1976: any of the last three syllables, lexically determined, oxytones commonest, proparoxytones rarest) and the GIEC 2016 statement already held; it also documents, in the field's own words, the 'regular vs lexical' framing that explains why StressTyp2 codes Catalan as quantity-sensitive (final-if-C-final else penult). It adds the note that the plural -s never attracts stress and that the same default extends to /n/-final stems after n-deletion.

One refinement: the same section (Art. 63 p. 8, algorithm (13b-c)) states the weight-based default explicitly — 'In the absence of lexical stress: b. Project a mora from a final consonant; c. sources.citation: Faust, Noam and Torres-Tamarit, Francesc (2017). Stress and final /n/ deletion in Catalan: Combining Strict CV and OT. Glossa: a journal of general linguistics 2(1): 63, 1-23.
sources.quote: In Catalan, nominal forms have either regular or lexical stress. Regular stress falls on the last vowel if the word is consonant-final (11a) and on the penultimate vowel if the word is vowel-final (11b). [...] Lexical stress can appear on any vowel within a right-oriented three-syllable window. Penultimate stress is exceptional in consonant-final words (12a), final stress is exceptional in vowel-final words (12b), and there are also words ending in a vowel or a consonant that show antepenultimate stress (12c). [...] Morphological structure is in most cases irrelevant for stress assignment.
sources.locator: §2.2 'Stress in Catalan', Art. 63 pp.7-8 (txt lines 999-1060), with tables (11)-(12) and algorithm (13); also §1 p.3 (txt line 175)
sources.note: Nominal stress = regular default (C-final -> final: [əlməˈnak], [pəˈtit]; V-final -> penult: [nəˈɣɔsi], [munˈtaɲə]) plus lexical stress anywhere in a right-edge three-syllable window ([kəˈpitul], [təˈβu], [məˈtɾɔpuli]); plural -s does not attract stress; stress-attracting but unstressed suffixes (-ic); most prior accounts (Cabré 1993, Serra 1996, Vallverdú 1997, Bonet & Lloret 1998) use a right-aligned moraic trochee with a final-consonant mora, which the authors replace by an empty-nucleus account. Also: 'final stress in Catalan is most commonly found in consonant-final words'.

sources.citation: Cabré, Teresa and Prieto, Pilar (2004). Prosodic and analogical effects in lexical glide formation in Catalan. Probus 16(1): 113-150.
sources.quote: Distance of the vocoid sequence from the main word stress is another factor which conditions glide formation: the greater the distance, the greater the tendency to pronounce a diphthong. [...] Glide formation in this context can be easily explained by the strong prosodic preference for trochaic feet (and the avoidance of antepenultimate stress) shown by the Catalan language: històr[iə] > històr[jə] 'history'; àv[iə] > àv[jə] 'grandmother'. [fn. 9:] Majorcan and Roussillon Catalan have resolved such historical antepenultimate stress patterns by deleting the final vowel: història → histori 'history', família → famili 'family'.
sources.note: Object is glide formation, conditioned by word-initial position and distance to the (lexically given) stressed syllable; presupposes lexical stress position and states that Catalan strongly prefers trochaic feet and avoids antepenultimate stress (post-tonic hiatus contracts; Majorcan/Roussillon delete the final vowel). No placement rule is stated.

sources.citation: Prieto, Pilar and Rigau, Gemma (2007). The syntax-prosody interface: Catalan interrogative sentences headed by que. Journal of Portuguese Linguistics 6(2): 29-59.
sources.quote: This article explores the syntactic and prosodic characteristics of polar questions headed by unstressed particles such as que 'that' or o 'or' in different Catalan dialects (vg. Que plou? 'Is it raining?'). The presence or absence of the conjunction, together with suprasegmental information, are used variously to encode a variety of systematic pragmatic meanings.
sources.locator: Abstract, p.29; intonation descriptions pp.31ff. (txt lines 267-271, 690, 723, 767, 952 mention only the 'last stressed syllable' as a tonal anchor)
sources.note: Intonation and syntax of que-headed polar questions across dialects; word stress appears only as the anchoring point of nuclear pitch movements ('the last stressed syllable in the utterance'). No statement of where word stress falls.

sources.citation: Vanrell, Maria del Mar, Armstrong, Meghan E. and Prieto, Pilar (2014). The role of prosody in the encoding of evidentiality in Catalan. Proceedings of the 7th International Conference on Speech Prosody (Dublin), 1022-1025.
sources.quote: Specifically, we aimed to investigate what type of meaning was encoded in yes-no questions through the combination of the question particle (QP) que 'that' and the nuclear intonational pattern L+H* L% in Majorcan Catalan yes-no questions (i.e., Que és un llibre?L+H* L% 'QP-It's a book?'), and to understand any temporal information that might be encoded through this construction.
sources.note: Majorcan Catalan intonation (nuclear pitch configuration + question particle) and evidential meaning; the word 'stress' does not occur in the text. Nothing on word-stress placement.

sources.citation: Astruc, Lluïsa & Pilar Prieto (2006). Acoustic cues of stress and accent in Catalan. Proc. Speech Prosody 2006, Dresden, paper 209. doi:10.21437/SpeechProsody.2006-83.

[Published as: Torres-Tamarit & Pons-Moll (2019). Enclitic-induced stress shift in Catalan. Journal of Linguistics 55(2): 407-444.]

sources.access_detail: open link recorded by Glottolog or the catalog, not checked
sources.quote: In this paper we provide a novel and unified formal analysis of the stress microvariation found in verb–enclitic groupings in Barcelona Catalan, with stress stability, in Formentera Catalan, with stress shift to the penultimate and the last syllable of the whole sequence, and in Mallorca and Menorca Catalan, with stress shift to the last syllable. We argue that stress shift in Formentera Catalan conforms directly to the unmarked pattern of nominal stress in Catalan, that is, a right-aligned moraic trochee, with the constraint All-Feet-Right undominated, leading to final and penultimate stress.
sources.locator: Published abstract (Crossref metadata and Cambridge Core product page for 10.1017/S0022226718000427)
sources.note: Verb+enclitic stress: stable in Barcelona Catalan, shifts to penult/final (Formentera) or to the final syllable (Mallorca, Menorca); treats the unmarked nominal stress pattern as a right-aligned moraic trochee giving final (C-final) or penultimate (V-final) stress. Adds Balearic clitic-group stress shift, which the catalog record does not mention.

sources.quote: This monograph presents an experimental and theoretical inquiry into the role of sentential form and variation in the prosodic structure of Catalan. The empirical section examines intonational phrasing across sentence forms, including SVO structures with either nominal or sentential objects and structures involving clitic left- and right-dislocations. The results show variation in phrasing that depends on syntactic factors and non-syntactic factors such as topic-hood and prosodic binarity.
sources.note: Intonational phrasing and its syntactic conditioning modelled in Stochastic OT; nothing on word-stress placement.
